<issue identifier="MM-453">
<title>Phase 0a: Mode-select honesty — "Create an identity" / "Import an identity" + non-Custos create gate</title>
<description>
Part of <issue id="d5cb6e3d-f781-4ecb-aebf-c954915b3708" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-452/obsign-without-custos-first-class-any-pds-wallet-support-epic">MM-452</issue>. Design: `docs/design-plans/2026-07-24-obsign-without-custos.md` §Phase 0a.

## Problem

`ModeSelectScreen.svelte` currently offers:

1. **"Add an identity"** → the create flow. Should read **"Create an identity"**.
2. **"Move an identity to another PDS"** → actually launches the **claim flow** (identity_input → pds_auth → review_operation), which takes sovereign custody of an identity that *stays on its current PDS*. The label describes a different feature (outbound migration lives on the identity detail screen) and hides the exact flow that is the front door for non-Custos users. Should read **"Import an identity"**.
3. "Recover from backup shares" — unchanged.

Sharper problem behind (1): `PdsConfigScreen` accepts any PDS URL, but the create flow is Custos-structural (`POST /v1/accounts/mobile` claim-code redeem, then the `/v1/dids` genesis ceremony — standard `createAccount` never lets the client author rotation keys). Pointing the config at a reference PDS today fails later with an opaque error.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Button copy updated as above; harness scenarios/tests and docs screenshots that assert the old strings updated with it.
2. When the configured PDS does not advertise the `createCeremony` Custos capability (per MM-454's probe; until that lands, gate on the probe's absence-of-`custos`-field fallback), the create flow entry explains honestly that creating a new identity requires a Custos server and steers to "Import an identity" instead — before the user has typed anything, not as a late network error.
3. The steer is a calm redirect, not an upsell wall: importing from the configured PDS must remain one tap away.
</description>

<id>d5cb6e3d-f781-4ecb-aebf-c954915b3708</id>
<title>Obsign without Custos — first-class any-PDS wallet support (epic)</title>
<description>
## Strategy

Broaden Obsign's market beyond Custos-hosted accounts: a user on the reference PDS, [bsky.social](<http://bsky.social>), or any spec-compliant PDS should get real, honest value from the wallet — Secure-Enclave root key, PLC monitoring + 72h override, user-held repo/media backup, self-held Shamir recovery — with Custos capabilities (escrow-assisted recovery, passwordless sovereign sessions, agents, wallet-confirmed consent) as the opt-in upgrade rather than a lock-in. Rescue and migration must never force a stressed user onto Custos.

Design doc: `docs/design-plans/2026-07-24-obsign-without-custos.md` (survey of what already works without Custos, the ecosystem describeServer survey, the capability-extension design, and phase rationale).

## As-built starting point (verified 2026-07-24, v0.8.1)

Already works on any PDS today: the claim/import flow (device key → `rotationKeys[0]` via standard lexicons), PLC monitoring + recovery override ([plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) only), repo + blob backup (public sync endpoints, no session), endpoint repair, sovereign share-based recovery (Shares 1+3), and disaster recovery **into a Custos destination**.

Custos-locked today: create ceremony, Shamir generation/re-key (fused to `/v1/dids` + escrow), sovereign sessions (and everything downstream: app passwords, change handle, removal, blob restore), agents/consent, and the rescue/migration **destination** (finalize unconditionally mints `/v1/sessions/sovereign`).

## Phases (one child issue each)

* Phase 0a — mode-select honesty: "Create an identity" / "Import an identity" + non-Custos create gate
* Phase 0b — `custos` capability extension in describeServer + self-identifying `_health`
* Phase 0c — positioning + live validation of the any-PDS arc (claim → backup → rescue)
* Phase 1 — self-held Shamir kit for foreign-hosted identities (escrow-less re-key)
* Phase 2 — foreign-PDS session provider (password `createSession` unlock path)
* Phase 3 — any-PDS rescue/migration destination (capability-gated finalize)

Parked (needs its own design pass, deliberately not in this epic): "create-then-sovereignize" — creating a brand-new account on a reference PDS via standard `createAccount` then immediately running the claim ceremony.
</description>
</parent-issue>
<issue-relations><related><issue-ref identifier="MM-455" title="Phase 0c: "Obsign for any PDS" positioning + live validation of the claim → backup → rescue arc"/></related></issue-relations>
</issue>

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- ed3d-basic-agents:haiku-general-purpose: An unprompted generic subagent. Uses Haiku. Intended for tasks that require less thinking and analysis. Good for summarization, research, and tool calls. (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-basic-agents:opus-general-purpose: An unprompted generic subagent. Uses Opus. Intended for tasks that require deep reasoning, complex analysis, or nuanced judgment. (Tools: All tools except Agent)
- ed3d-basic-agents:sonnet-general-purpose: An unprompted generic subagent. Uses Sonnet. Intended for tasks that require attention to detail, thinking, and analysis. (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-extending-claude:project-claude-librarian: Use when completing development phases and project context files may need updating - analyzes what changed since phase start, identifies affected CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md files, and coordinates updates to maintain accurate project documentation (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-plan-and-execute:code-reviewer: Reviews completed project steps against plans and enforces coding standards. Use when a numbered step from a plan is complete, a major feature is implemented, or before creating a PR. Validates plan alignment, code quality, test coverage, and architecture. Blocks merges for Minor, Important, or Critical issues. (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-plan-and-execute:task-bug-fixer: Fixes issues identified by code-reviewer and triggers re-review. Use when code-reviewer returns any issues that need to be addressed before merge approval. (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-plan-and-execute:task-implementor-fast: Implements individual tasks from plans with TDD, skill application, verification, and git commits. Use when executing a specific task that requires writing, modifying, or testing code as part of a larger plan. (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-plan-and-execute:test-analyst: Use after final code review passes to validate test coverage against acceptance criteria and generate human test plans - reads test-requirements.md, verifies automated tests exist, produces manual verification documentation (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-playwright:playwright-explorer: Use when exploring websites, proving hypotheses about web application behavior, automating browser interactions, or generating E2E tests - investigates page structure through accessibility snapshots, tests assumptions systematically, and coordinates Playwright MCP tools with tenacity to complete complex multi-step investigations (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-research-agents:codebase-investigator: Use this agent when planning or designing features and you need to understand current codebase state, find existing patterns, or verify assumptions about what exists. Examples: <example>Context: Starting brainstorming phase and need to understand current authentication implementation. user: "I want to add OAuth support to our app" assistant: "Let me use the codebase-investigator agent to understand how authentication currently works before we design the OAuth integration" <commentary>Before designing new features, investigate existing patterns to ensure the design builds on what's already there.</commentary></example> <example>Context: Writing implementation plan and need to verify file locations and current structure. user: "Create a plan for adding user profiles" assistant: "I'll use the codebase-investigator agent to verify the current user model structure and find where user-related code lives" <commentary>Investigation prevents hallucinating file paths or assuming structure that doesn't exist.</commentary></example> (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-research-agents:combined-researcher: Use this agent when planning or designing features and you need current information BOTH the local system AND from the internet, API documentation, library usage patterns, or external knowledge. Examples: <example>Context: Designing integration with external service and need to understand current API. user: "I want to integrate with the Stripe API for payments" assistant: "Let me use the combined-researcher agent to find if and how we currently use Stripe, and then the current Stripe API documentation and best practices for integration" <commentary>Before designing integrations, research current API state and current local codebase state to ensure plan matches reality.</commentary></example> <example>Context: Evaluating technology choices for implementation plan. user: "Should we use library X or Y for this feature?" assistant: "I'll use the combined-researcher agent to research what we've currently selected already, then if we haven't selected something we'll look at both libraries' current status, features, and community recommendations" <commentary>Research helps make informed technology decisions based on current information.</commentary></example> (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-research-agents:internet-researcher: Use this agent when planning or designing features and you need current information from the internet, API documentation, library usage patterns, or external knowledge. Examples: <example>Context: Designing integration with external service and need to understand current API. user: "I want to integrate with the Stripe API for payments" assistant: "Let me use the internet-researcher agent to find the current Stripe API documentation and best practices for integration" <commentary>Before designing integrations, research current API state to ensure plan matches reality.</commentary></example> <example>Context: Evaluating technology choices for implementation plan. user: "Should we use library X or Y for this feature?" assistant: "I'll use the internet-researcher agent to research both libraries' current status, features, and community recommendations" <commentary>Research helps make informed technology decisions based on current information.</commentary></example> (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-research-agents:remote-code-researcher: Use when understanding how external libraries or open-source projects implement features by examining actual source code - finds repos via web search, clones to a stable cache directory, investigates with codebase analysis. Triggers: "how does library X implement Y", "show me how Z handles this", "I want to see the actual code for", evaluating library internals before adoption. (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-session-reflection:conversation-reviewer: Use when reviewing a Claude Code session transcript for quality — analyzes human prompting effectiveness, agent performance patterns, and environment/tooling gaps, then writes structured findings to a specified output file. Requires a reduced transcript path and output path. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill)

- episodic-memory:search-conversations: Gives you memory across sessions. You don't automatically remember past conversations - THIS AGENT RESTORES IT. Search your history before starting any task to recover decisions, solutions, and lessons learned. (Tools: Read, mcp__plugin_episodic-memory_episodic-memory__search, mcp__plugin_episodic-memory_episodic-memory__show)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by doing a git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. 

Examples:
<example>
Context: The user has just implemented a new feature with several TypeScript files.
user: "I've added the new authentication feature. Can you check if everything looks good?"
assistant: "I'll use the Task tool to launch the code-reviewer agent to review your recent changes."
<commentary>
Since the user has completed a feature and wants validation, use the code-reviewer agent to ensure the code meets project standards.
</commentary>
</example>
<example>

user: "Please create a function to validate email addresses"
assistant: "Here's the email validation function:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
assistant: "Now I'll use the Task tool to launch the code-reviewer agent to review this implementation."
<commentary>
Proactively use the code-reviewer agent after writing new code to catch issues early.
</commentary>
</example>

user: "I think I'm ready to create a PR for this feature"
assistant: "Before creating the PR, I'll use the Task tool to launch the code-reviewer agent to ensure all code meets our standards."
<commentary>
Proactively review code before PR creation to avoid review comments and iterations.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"

After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.

assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

152-unchanged (its epilogue skips re-escrow on hosts without the `escrow`
153-capability). The upsell seam is a single post-completion prompt, not pressure.
154-
155-### Phase 2 — foreign-PDS sessions ([MM-457](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-457))
156-
157-`SessionProvider`'s `NeedsUnlock` gains a second resolution: on hosts without
158-`sovereignSessions`, a password `createSession` prompt (the transient machinery
159-`source_login.rs` already uses), persisting the Bearer pair in the same
160-versioned `{did}:oauth-tokens` record so the provider's refresh ladder is
161-unchanged. This lights up app passwords, change handle, identity removal, and
162-blob restore for foreign identities — all already standard-lexicon features that
163-are dark only for want of a session. ADR-0021's full-session requirement and the
164-use-once-never-store password posture both hold.
165-
166-### Phase 3 — any-PDS rescue destination ([MM-458](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-458))
167-
168-`finalize_migration_core`'s injected `ensure_session` step branches on the
169-destination's `sovereignSessions` capability: present → today's sovereign-session
170-mint; absent → durably persist the Bearer session already held from the
171-migration `createAccount`, preserving the strict
172-activate → durable-credential → deactivate ordering. One branch serves both
173-sovereign disaster recovery to a non-Custos destination and outbound migration
174-between arbitrary hosts. This is a deliberate strategic choice: the rescue path
175-must not be a lock-in funnel, which paradoxically strengthens the Custos pitch —
176-conversion happens because escrow/agents/consent are worth it, with trust intact.
177-
178-## Sequencing and rationale
179-
180-0a/0b/0c are cheap and independent (0a's gate consumes 0b's probe but has a
181-degraded interim form). Phase 1 completes the "benefits without Custos" story —

<script lang="ts">
  import { onMount } from 'svelte';
  import { savePdsUrl, getPdsUrl, type PdsConfigError } from '$lib/ipc';
  import OnboardingShell from '$lib/components/ui/OnboardingShell.svelte';
  import TextField from '$lib/components/ui/TextField.svelte';
  import Button from '$lib/components/ui/Button.svelte';
  import Spinner from '$lib/components/ui/Spinner.svelte';

  const DEFAULT_PDS_URL = 'https://obsign.org';

  let { onnext, onback = undefined }: { onnext: () => void; onback?: () => void } = $props();

  let url = $state(DEFAULT_PDS_URL);
  let loading = $state(false);
  let error = $state<string | undefined>(undefined);

  // Seed the field from the currently-saved PDS URL (if any) so the user sees the host that is
  // actually active, instead of always seeing the built-in default. The active URL is restored
  // from the Keychain at launch and is otherwise invisible — which made a stale/wrong host
  // (e.g. a previous staging URL) impossible to notice.
  onMount(() => {
    const initialUrl = url;
    void (async () => {
      try {
        const saved = await getPdsUrl();
        // Only hydrate if the user hasn't started editing while the IPC call was in flight,
        // otherwise a late resolve would clobber their input.
        if (saved && url === initialUrl) url = saved;
      } catch (e) {
        console.warn('[PdsConfigScreen] failed to load saved PDS URL:', e);
      }
    })();
  });

  let isValidFormat = $derived(
    url.trim().length > 0 &&
      (url.startsWith('http://') || url.startsWith('https://'))
  );

  async function handleConnect() {
    error = undefined;
    loading = true;
    try {
      await savePdsUrl(url.trim());
      onnext();
    } catch (e) {
      const err = e as PdsConfigError;
      if (err.code === 'INVALID_URL') {
        error = 'Invalid URL — must start with http:// or https://';
      } else if (err.code === 'KEYCHAIN_ERROR') {
        error = 'Could not save the server URL. Please try again.';
      } else {
        error = 'Could not reach the server. Check the URL and try again.';
      }
    } finally {
      loading = false;
    }
  }
</script>

<OnboardingShell
  {onback}
  title="Connect to Custos"
  subtitle="Your wallet connects to a server to create your identity. Use the default, or enter the address of your own."
>
  <TextField
    bind:value={url}
    type="url"
    mono
    disabled={loading}
    placeholder="https://obsign.org"
    autocomplete="off"
    autocorrect="off"
    autocapitalize="off"
    spellcheck={false}
    aria-label="Server URL"
    {error}
  />
  {#if loading}
    <Spinner label="Connecting…" />
  {:else}
    <Button disabled={!isValidFormat} onclick={handleConnect}>Connect</Button>
  {/if}
</OnboardingShell>

# Obsign (identity-wallet) Mobile App

Last verified: 2026-07-08
Last updated: 2026-07-20

## Purpose

Tauri v2 iOS application — SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5 frontend running in a native WKWebView, communicating with a Rust backend exclusively through Tauri's IPC bridge.

## Browser test harness (drive the app without a simulator)

The whole frontend runs in a plain desktop browser under `vite dev` — the only thing the
browser lacks is the Tauri `invoke()` seam, which the harness intercepts with Tauri's
official `mockIPC`. This lets an agent (or a human) reach every screen and reproduce any
state, including rare error states, without a Mac/Xcode/simulator. Design + acceptance
criteria: [docs/archive/design-plans/2026-07-12-browser-harness.md](../../docs/archive/design-plans/2026-07-12-browser-harness.md).

**Start it** (or use the `.claude/launch.json` config `wallet-harness` / `wallet-harness-proxy`):
- **Fake mode** (default, no backend needed): `pnpm --dir apps/identity-wallet dev:harness` → http://localhost:5173.
- **Proxy mode** (real thin-HTTP calls against a hermetic local PDS): in one terminal
  `cargo build -p pds` then `just harness-pds` (prints the URL + admin token); in another,
  `VITE_HARNESS_PDS_URL=<url> VITE_HARNESS_ADMIN_TOKEN=<token> pnpm --dir apps/identity-wallet dev:harness:proxy`.
- Plain `pnpm dev` never activates the harness (double-gated on `import.meta.env.DEV && VITE_HARNESS`);
  `pnpm check:harness-absence` proves it is tree-shaken out of production builds.

**`window.__harness` console API** (both modes):
- `.scenario(name)` — switch preset and reload (persists across reload). Presets:
  `fresh-install`, `one-identity`, `multi-identity`, `alert-active`, `migration-in-flight`,
  `agent-connected`, `app-password-minted`, plus the share-recovery matrix:
  `recover-escrow` (happy path A — iCloud Share 1 + zero-delay escrow release),
  `recover-sovereign` (happy path B — manual Share 3 entry; paste
  `state().recovery.fixtures.share3Words` or `.share3`), `recover-wrong-set`
  (`fixtures.wrongSet` → SHARE_SET_MISMATCH), `recover-corrupt-share`
  (`fixtures.corrupt` → SHARE_CHECKSUM), `recover-mismatch` (verification fails —
  shares don't match the identity), `recover-pending-delay` (24h escrow window; the
  second poll releases), `recover-cancelled` (pending release cancelled → uniform
  401 on poll), `recover-epilogue-resume` (launch resumes an interrupted rotation
  epilogue). `.scenarios` lists them.
- `.failNext(command, error)` — make the next call of `command` reject with a typed error,
  e.g. `window.__harness.failNext('create_account', { code: 'EXPIRED_CODE' })`.
- `.emit(event, payload)` — deliver a Tauri event to live `listen()` subscribers;
  `window.__harness.emit('auth_ready')` simulates the OAuth deep-link return.
- `.state()` — a read-only snapshot of the fake store. `.mode` is `'fake'` or `'proxy'`.

**Proxy mode is real only for the thin-HTTP subset** — `create_account` (mints + redeems a
real claim code, POSTs `/v1/accounts/mobile`) and `get_available_user_domains`
(describeServer). By the honest boundary, these stay **faked even in proxy mode** (heavy
Rust logic with no thin-HTTP form): the DID ceremony (`perform_did_ceremony`,
`*_did_web_ceremony`), OAuth completion (`prepare/complete_oauth_flow`), the migration
transfer legs (`transfer_repo`/`transfer_blobs`/…, `finalize_migration`), recovery/claim
PLC ops, and the agent surfaces (which need a real post-ceremony session the faked
ceremony never mints). Fidelity the browser can never cover: real Keychain/Secure-Enclave,
the biometric prompt, ASWebAuthenticationSession, WKWebView rendering, safe-area insets,
camera/QR — those stay simulator/device concerns.

**Fake handler coverage is enforced:** every command in `$lib/ipc` must have a handler in
`src/lib/harness/registry.ts` or `registry.test.ts` fails (`pnpm test`). Harness code lives
in `src/lib/harness/` (`install`/`registry`/`state`/`scenarios`/`control` + `proxy/`),
activated by `src/hooks.client.ts`.

## Contracts

### Frontend (SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5)

**Exposes:**
- `src/lib/ipc/` — per-domain typed wrappers for all Tauri IPC commands, re-exported from `src/lib/ipc/index.ts`; import from `$lib/ipc` instead of calling `invoke()` directly. Exports: `createAccount()`, `performDIDCeremony()`, `registerHandle()`, `getAvailableUserDomains()`, `registerCreatedIdentity()`, `startOAuthFlow()`, `getPdsUrl()`, `savePdsUrl()`, `getAppearancePreference()`, `setAppearancePreference()`, `resolveIdentity()`, `authenticateSourcePds()`, `requestClaimVerification()`, `signAndVerifyClaim()`, `submitClaim()`, `listIdentities()`, `getStoredDidDoc()`, `getDeviceKeyId()`, `checkIdentityStatus()`, `buildRecoveryOverride()`, `submitRecoveryOverride()`, and their associated types (`CreateAccountResult`, `CreateAccountError`, `DIDCeremonyResult`, `DIDCeremonyError`, `RegisterHandleResult`, `RegisterHandleError`, `RegisterIdentityError`, `OAuthError`, `PdsConfigError`, `AppearancePreference`, `AppearanceError`, `IdentityInfo`, `VerifiedClaimOp`, `OpDiff`, `ServiceChange`, `ClaimResult`, `ResolveError`, `ClaimError`, `IdentityStoreError`, `UnauthorizedChange`, `IdentityStatus`, `SignedRecoveryOp`, `RecoveryError`, `SignedMigrationOp`, `MigrateError`) and migration wrappers (`buildMigrationOp()`, `submitMigrationOp()`) and outbound-migration orchestrator wrappers (`prepareMigration()`, `authenticateMigrationSource()`, `createDestinationAccount()`, `transferRepo()`, `transferBlobs(did, acceptLoss)`, `transferPreferences()`, `verifyImport()`, `armIdentityLeg()`, `finalizeMigration()`) with types (`AccountStatus`, `PreparedMigration`, `MigrationError`, `BlobLoss`, `BlobTransferDirection`), the sovereign change-handle wrappers (`getIdentityHandleDomains()`, `changeHandle()` — biometric-gated) with type `HandleChangeError`, and identity-removal wrappers (`requestIdentityRemoval()`, `confirmIdentityRemoval()`, `tombstoneIdentity()`, `listPendingRemovals()`, `forgetIdentityLocally()`) with types (`RemovalError`, `RemovalOutcome`), and the share-recovery wrappers (`startShareRecovery()`, `addRecoveryShare()`, `removeRecoveryShare()`, `initiateEscrowRelease()`, `requestEscrowRelease()`, `verifyRecoveryShares()`, `recoverIdentity()` — biometric-gated, `runRecoveryEpilogue()`, `getPendingRecoveryEpilogue()`, `confirmRecoveryBackup()`) with types (`ShareRecoveryError`, `CollectedShare`, `RecoveryTarget`, `EscrowReleaseStatus`, `RecoveredIdentity`, `RecoveryAnchor`, `EpilogueResult`, `PendingEpilogue`), and the media-backup wrappers (`getBlobBackupStatus()`, `setBlobBackupEnabled()`, `runBlobBackup()`, `restoreBlobBackup()` — biometric-gated, and the app-global background-sweep settings `getBackgroundBackupSettings()` / `setBackgroundBackupSettings()`) with types (`BlobBackupStatus`, `BlobBackupRunReport`, `BlobRestoreReport`, `BlobFailure`, `BackupLocation`, `BlobBackupError`, `BackgroundBackupSettings`, `BackgroundBackupError`), and the repo-backup wrappers (`getRepoBackupStatus()`, `setRepoBackupEnabled()`, `runRepoBackup()`, `exportRepoBackup()` — none biometric-gated; all read the public `getRepo` or local disk) with types (`RepoBackupStatus`, `RepoBackupRunReport`, `RepoExport`, `RepoBackupError`)
- `src/lib/components/onboarding/` — one screen component per step of the create / import / recover onboarding flows (the directory listing is the authoritative inventory; hand-counted lists here drifted twice)
- `src/lib/components/home/` — the home-surface screen components (the directory listing is the authoritative inventory) plus the DIDAvatar utility component (deterministic DID-derived hue circle). ChangeHandleScreen is the sovereign change-handle surface reached from DIDDocumentScreen's "Change handle" button (did:plc + device-key-as-root only): it loads the hosting PDS's served domains, pre-flights the session (`ensureIdentitySession`, passwordless `sovereignLogin` on `NEEDS_UNLOCK`), then runs the biometric-gated `changeHandle`. AppPasswordsScreen is the app-password surface reached from DIDDocumentScreen's "Sign in to Bluesky and other apps" button: it lists/mints/revokes the account's scoped app passwords via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` (SESSION_LOCKED → `sovereignLogin` + retry; mint and revoke are biometric-gated; the generated secret is shown once with copy and never persisted). MediaBackupScreen is the user-held blob-backup surface reached from DIDDocumentScreen's "Back up media" button: opt-in with the mirror size always shown, "Back up now" (incremental, CID-verified sync pass over public sync endpoints — no session), and a biometric-gated "Restore to server" (`uploadBlob` via `SessionProvider::full_access_client`; SESSION_LOCKED → `sovereignLogin` + retry), with per-blob failures listed rather than aborting the run. The same screen also holds a "Back up your posts" section (`repo_backup.rs`): opt-in with the snapshot size + last-backup shown, and "Back up posts now" (a full-CAR `getRepo` snapshot, validated client-side before it replaces the prior copy — no session, no biometric); there is no repo "restore" button (an `importRepo` needs a deactivated account, so restore flows through migration). `+page.svelte` fires silent opportunistic `runBlobBackup` **and** `runRepoBackup` passes on app open for opted-in identities (each on its own per-DID flag). MyAgentsScreen is the agent list; AgentDetailScreen is the per-agent sub-view (audit-trail paging + biometric-gated revoke) it renders on selection, its lifetime scoped to that selection. RemoveIdentityScreen is the permanent-removal flow (warn → emailed-code + password → biometric-gated hold-to-remove → progress, with a "tombstone pending, retry" state), reached from DIDDocumentScreen's destructive `onremove`
- `src/lib/appearance.ts` — in-app appearance override (System / Light / Dark): `normalizePreference()` / `toColorScheme()` (pure, tested by `appearance.test.ts`), `readLocalMirror()`, `initAppearance()` (launch-time reconcile: re-asserts the localStorage mirror, then reads the Keychain via IPC and lets it win), `setAppearance()` (applies the inline `color-scheme` override on `<html>` instantly, writes the mirror, then persists to the Keychain). The localStorage mirror (key `appearance-preference`) exists only so `src/app.html`'s inline `<head>` script can apply a forced appearance before first paint; the Keychain is the source of truth
- `src/lib/agent-scopes.ts` — plain-language descriptions of granular OAuth scope tokens for the agent-consent surfaces: `describeScope(token)` / `describeScopes(tokens)` return `{ summary, token, elevated }` (the raw token is always shown alongside the human sentence; `account:*`/`identity:*`/full-access grants are flagged `elevated`; an unknown token falls back to showing itself, never a vague label). Tested by `agent-scopes.test.ts`
- `src/lib/deadline.ts` — PLC recovery deadline utilities: `getDeadline(createdAt)` (adds 72h to ISO 8601 timestamp), `getUrgency(deadline)` (returns `'safe'` | `'warning'` | `'critical'` | `'expired'`), `formatCountdown(deadline)` (human-readable `"Xh Ym remaining"`). `Urgency` type exported. Thresholds: expired = 0, critical < 4h, warning < 24h, safe >= 24h
- `src/routes/+page.svelte` — root page: two-flow state machine starting at `mode_select`. **Create flow:** mode_select -> pds_config -> claim_code -> email -> handle -> password (every pre-submit step wires `onback` to the previous step) -> loading -> did_ceremony -> did_success -> shamir_backup -> handle_registration -> complete -> authenticating -> home (after handle_registration succeeds, `finishCreateFlow()` calls `registerCreatedIdentity()` to persist the new identity to `IdentityStore` so it appears in `IdentityListHome` — best-effort, never blocks the flow). **Import flow:** mode_select -> identity_input -> pds_auth -> email_verification -> review_operation -> claim_success -> home. **Home:** home -> identity_detail -> { change_handle | alert_detail -> recovery_override }. On mount, checks for existing identities via `listIdentities()` and skips to `home` if any exist. Registers a `visibilitychange` listener that calls `checkIdentityStatus()` when the app returns to foreground while on the `home` step

**Guarantees:**
- SSR is disabled globally (`ssr = false` in `src/routes/+layout.ts`); the frontend is a fully static SPA loaded from disk by WKWebView
- Build output lands in `dist/` (configured via `pages: 'dist'` in `svelte.config.js`)
- Frontend calls Tauri commands only through the `src/lib/ipc/` modules (imported from `$lib/ipc`) — no raw `invoke()` calls in page components
- PDS error codes from `create_account` are mapped back to the originating screen (e.g. EXPIRED_CODE -> claim_code step, EMAIL_TAKEN -> email step)

**Expects:**
- `pnpm install` has been run in `apps/identity-wallet/`
- Node.js 22.x is in PATH (provided by the Nix dev shell)

### Rust Backend (src-tauri/)

**Exposes:**
- `src/lib.rs::create_account(claim_code, email, handle) -> Result<CreateAccountResult, CreateAccountError>` — Tauri IPC command: gets or creates device key via `device_key::get_or_create()`, POSTs to PDS `/v1/accounts/mobile`, stores tokens in Keychain on success
- `src/lib.rs::perform_did_ceremony(handle: String, password: String) -> Result<DIDCeremonyResult, DIDCeremonyError>` — Tauri IPC command running the **client-share ceremony** (ceremony inversion): fetches the PDS signing key (GET /v1/repo-signing-key), loads-or-generates the client-side share set via `share_ceremony::load_or_create` (recovery seed + `derive_recovery_keypair` + 2-of-3 v2 envelope split, staged in the `ceremony-staging` Keychain slot BEFORE any network call so a retry reuses the identical set/set_id), builds the signed did:plc genesis op via `crypto::build_did_plc_genesis_op_multi_rotation_with_external_signer` with `rotationKeys = [device, recovery, PDS]` (ADR-0027) using the device key as signer, POSTs the op + password + `recoveryKey` + `escrowShare` (the Share 2 envelope — the only share Custos ever sees) to POST /v1/dids, persists DID + upgraded session token in Keychain, writes the wallet-generated Share 1 envelope to the per-DID slot `recovery-share-1:{did}` with a read-back verify (same convention as the re-key flow, so a second identity's ceremony cannot overwrite the first's Share 1), and returns `{ did, share3, share3Words }` to the frontend
- `src/lib.rs::confirm_share_backup(did: String) -> Result<(), ShareBackupError>` — Tauri IPC command: the ceremony teardown gate. Verifies the ceremony DID's Share 1 is durably present in `recovery-share-1:{did}` (else `SHARE_NOT_STORED` — the staging slot must not be destroyed while it is the seed's only home), then deletes the `ceremony-staging` slot (the seed's and Share 2's last local copy). The `did` is threaded from the ceremony result so the check reads the exact identity just created (mirrors the re-key epilogue's `confirm_rekey`). Idempotent; invoked by the frontend when the Shamir backup screen's confirmation completes
- `src/share_ceremony.rs` — client-side share generation module: `CeremonyShareSet` (recovery key did:key + the three base32 envelope strings + the Share 3 word phrase, all share material in `Zeroizing`), `load_or_create(handle, pds_url)` (reuse a valid staged set or generate + stage a fresh one; the staging record stores the three envelopes only — the seed is recomputed via `combine_envelopes(share1, share2)` on load), `clear_staging()` (idempotent teardown), `STAGING_ACCOUNT` (`"ceremony-staging"`). **Fail-closed staging contract:** only a genuinely absent slot, or one staged for different ceremony inputs (a new handle/PDS is the user's explicit abandonment of the old attempt), permits fresh generation; a present-but-unreadable/corrupt record errors with `StagingCorrupt` and preserves the slot — it may be the exact set a prior attempt already bound to a genesis op and escrowed, so overwriting it would permanently destroy the recovery seed
- `src/share_recovery.rs` — the "Recover existing identity" ceremony (10 Tauri IPC commands), the consuming inverse of `share_ceremony.rs`: `start_share_recovery(identifier)` (resolve handle/did:plc via plc.directory, then auto-load Share 1 from the resolved DID's per-DID slot `recovery-share-1:{did}`, falling back to the legacy global `recovery-share-1`, when it holds a valid v2 envelope), `add_recovery_share(share)` (base32 or word-phrase entry; SHARE_CHECKSUM, SHARE_SET_MISMATCH — with both set_ids — and DUPLICATE_SHARE are distinct, pre-combine errors), `remove_recovery_share(index)`, the escrow-assisted path client `initiate_escrow_release()` / `request_escrow_release(otp?)` (targets the account's own PDS endpoint from the authoritative DID state; OTP opens the release, OTP-less calls poll the pending window; the server's uniform 401 maps to RELEASE_UNAUTHORIZED), `verify_recovery_shares()` (combine → `derive_recovery_keypair` → compare against the **authoritative plc.directory audit log**, never a cached doc — mismatch is SHARES_DO_NOT_MATCH_IDENTITY, before anything signs), `recover_identity()` (fresh per-DID device key; the recovery key signs the rotation op installing it at `rotationKeys[0]`; talks ONLY to plc.directory — the fully-sovereign path makes zero PDS requests until re-escrow; idempotent on retry; durably stages the epilogue before returning), `run_recovery_epilogue(skip_escrow?)` (resumable: swap the new recovery key into `rotationKeys[1]` signed by the new device key → re-escrow the new Share 2 over a stored-or-fresh device-key sovereign session → rewrite the recovered DID's per-DID slot `recovery-share-1:{did}` with read-back verify; each step recorded in the durable `recovery-epilogue` Keychain record as it completes), `get_pending_recovery_epilogue()` (launch-time resume hook), `confirm_recovery_backup()` (teardown gate mirroring `confirm_share_backup`; destroys the epilogue record only after the NEW Share 1 is verified durable in the per-DID slot). Session state (`AppState.share_recovery_state`) is in-memory by design — the pre-anchor phase restarts from the entry screen; only the epilogue persists. `ShareRecoveryError` serializes as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` with camelCase fields
- `src/lib.rs::{prepare_did_web_ceremony,complete_did_web_ceremony}` — did:web sibling ceremony: obtains the same device key and pending account's reserved repo key, lets the frontend compose/export the reviewed `did.json`, then submits it to `POST /v1/dids` only after it is externally resolvable. Completion persists the upgraded session and the server-returned Shamir Share 1 into the per-DID slot `recovery-share-1:{did}` (the same convention as the client-share and re-key paths); managed-hosting selection then opts the account into `/v1/did-web/hosting`.
- `src/oauth.rs` — OAuth PKCE client module: `AppState` (pending_login + oauth_session mutexes + custos_client OnceLock + pds_client + claim_state + recovery_state + migration_state + orchestration_state; both source logins — the claim flow and the outbound migration — are password-based `createSession`, so neither parks OAuth state — see `claim::authenticate_source_pds` / `migration_orchestrator::authenticate_migration_source`), `OAuthSession` (access/refresh/expiry/nonce), `DPoPKeypair` (P-256, persisted in Keychain), `OAuthError` enum, PKCE utilities (verifier + S256 challenge), `OAuthPrepared` (the `{authUrl, callbackScheme}` returned to the frontend), `prepare_oauth_flow` + `complete_oauth_flow` (the create-flow login split around the in-app auth session: prepare does DPoP keygen/PKCE/PAR → authorize URL and parks the verifier+CSRF in `pending_login`; complete validates the callback URL + does the token exchange), `parse_callback_url` (shared callback-URL parser, `pub(crate)`); `AppState::pds_client()` accessor exposes `PdsClient` for claim flow commands
- `src/claim.rs` — PLC rotation key claim flow module (5 Tauri IPC commands): `resolve_identity(handle_or_did) -> Result<IdentityInfo, ResolveError>` (resolves handle/DID to identity info via plc.directory, stores ClaimState), `authenticate_source_pds(did, identifier, password, auth_factor_token?) -> Result<(), ClaimError>` (**password `createSession`** against the source PDS → full-session Bearer `OAuthClient` stored in ClaimState; the next steps are PLC/identity ops that no OAuth `transition:generic` token can drive, so a full session is required — ADR-0021/MM-289; the password is used once and never stored. An email-2FA account returns `TwoFactorRequired` on the token-less attempt — the PDS emails a code and the UI re-invokes with `auth_factor_token`), `request_claim_verification(did) -> Result<(), ClaimError>` (calls `requestPlcOperationSignature` XRPC on old PDS to trigger email verification), `sign_and_verify_claim(did, token) -> Result<VerifiedClaimOp, ClaimError>` (calls `getRecommendedDidCredentials` and `signPlcOperation` on old PDS, fetches audit log, verifies signature + 4-point local checks, stores signed op in ClaimState), `submit_claim(did) -> Result<ClaimResult, ClaimError>` (POSTs signed op to plc.directory, persists identity to IdentityStore, clears ClaimState). Types: `IdentityInfo`, `VerifiedClaimOp`, `OpDiff`, `ServiceChange`, `ClaimResult`, `ClaimState`. Error enums: `ResolveError` (HANDLE_NOT_FOUND, DID_NOT_FOUND, PDS_UNREACHABLE, NETWORK_ERROR), `ClaimError` (INVALID_TOKEN, VERIFICATION_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, UNAUTHORIZED, SOURCE_AUTH_FAILED, TWO_FACTOR_REQUIRED, ACCOUNT_MISMATCH, INSECURE_SOURCE_URL, INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE, RATE_LIMITED, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR)
- `src/oauth_client.rs` — `OAuthClient`: authenticated HTTP client supporting two auth modes selected at construction (private `AuthMode` enum): `new(session, base_url)` builds a **DPoP** client (wraps every request with `Authorization: DPoP {access_token}` + a `DPoP` proof header, transparent lazy refresh when the token has <60s remaining, automatic retry on `use_dpop_nonce` 400 responses); `new_bearer(access_jwt, refresh_jwt, base_url)` builds a **Bearer** client (`Authorization: Bearer {access_jwt}`, no DPoP proof/nonce dance, expiry derived from the access JWT's `exp` claim) — used for the migration destination-PDS session, which is created via a service-auth `createAccount` rather than an OAuth flow. Public API: `add_identity(did)` (registers DID in managed-dids index), `remove_identity(did)` (deletes DID and all per-DID entries), `list_identities()` (returns managed DIDs), `get_or_create_device_key(did)` (lazy per-DID P-256 key generation), `adopt_global_device_key(did)` (aliases the per-DID device key to the global `device_key.rs` key by copying its Keychain material into the per-DID slot — used by the create flow, whose genesis op is signed with the global key before the DID exists), `store_did_doc(did, json)` / `get_did_doc(did)` (DID document persistence), `store_plc_log(did, json)` / `get_plc_log(did)` (PLC audit log persistence), and `store_oauth_tokens(did, record)` / `load_oauth_tokens(did)` / `delete_oauth_tokens(did)` for the versioned full-access Bearer session in `{did}:oauth-tokens`. All methods require DID to be registered first (returns `IdentityNotFound` otherwise). `IdentityStoreError` enum: IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, IDENTITY_ALREADY_EXISTS, KEYCHAIN_ERROR, KEY_GENERATION_FAILED, SERIALIZATION_ERROR (serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }`)
- `src/sovereign_session.rs` — per-DID Custos sovereign login: discovers the selected DID's current PDS and server DID, signs the shared canonical envelope with that DID's device key, validates the response DID and JWT subject/audience, persists a versioned `SovereignTokenRecord`, and exposes `stored_bearer_client(did)` for authenticated XRPC helpers. `sovereign_login` is the narrow Tauri command; the typed frontend `sovereignLogin(did)` wrapper performs the biometric gate before invoking it. The `pub(crate)` JWT/audience helpers (`bearer_jwt_claims`, `audience_matches_server`) are the single source of the sub/aud binding check, reused by `session_provider`.
- `src/session_provider.rs` — per-DID full-access **session lifecycle** (the seam every authenticated Custos-hosted operation goes through; MM-305's minimum contract). `SessionProvider::full_access_client(pds_client, store, did, now) -> Result<ActiveSession, SessionError>` runs a decision ladder under a per-DID coalescing lock: (1) no record / dead refresh → `NeedsUnlock{NoRefreshChain}`; (2) access JWT still valid (`exp > now + 120s`) → rebuild a Bearer client **with no network** (this is what makes a restart or offline launch with a live token need no prompt); (3) near-expiry with a live refresh → discover the DID's current PDS, and if the host moved **discard the old-audience record** + `NeedsUnlock{HostChanged}`, else call `com.atproto.server.refreshSession` exactly once and atomically persist the rotated pair (re-validating sub/aud). Distinct terminal errors, never looped: `NeedsUnlock{reason}`, `RateLimited{retryAfter}`, `UnsupportedHost`, `Offline{message}`, `ServerFailure{status}`, `Keychain`, `InvalidResponse`. A revoked refresh (400/401) and a host change both delete the dead record; a rate limit keeps it. Coalescing is a re-read (not a shared future): the second caller for one DID waits on the lock, then re-loads the freshly-persisted record — so a refresh token can never be raced into replay detection. Does NOT reuse `OAuthClient::refresh_token_bearer` (which is in-memory-only by design) — the provider owns refresh+persist. Types: `ActiveSession` { client, did, pds_url, access_expires_at, refresh_expires_at, rotated }, `SessionReady` (serializable summary, drops the client), `UnlockReason` (NO_REFRESH_CHAIN / REFRESH_REVOKED / HOST_CHANGED), `SessionError` (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE `code`). The coalescing lock registry is a process-global `OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<did, Arc<tokio::Mutex>>>>` (unit-struct-over-global shape, like `IdentityStore`).
- `src/pds_client.rs` — PDS discovery and OAuth module for arbitrary PDS endpoints (not just our PDS). `PdsClient` struct (stateless, wraps a `reqwest::Client` + plc.directory URL). Public API: `plc_directory_url() -> &str` (returns the plc.directory base URL), `client() -> &Client` (returns the inner reqwest client), `resolve_handle(handle) -> Result<String, PdsClientError>` (DNS TXT `_atproto.{handle}` with HTTP `/.well-known/atproto-did` fallback), `discover_pds(did) -> Result<(String, PlcDidDocument), PdsClientError>` (fetches DID doc from plc.directory, extracts `atproto_pds` endpoint, verifies reachability via HEAD), `discover_auth_server(pds_url) -> Result<AuthServerMetadata, PdsClientError>` (fetches `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, validates `code` response type + S256 challenge method), `pds_par(metadata, pkce_challenge, state, dpop_proof, dpop_jkt, login_hint?) -> Result<PdsParResponse, PdsClientError>` (PAR to arbitrary PDS), `pds_token_exchange(metadata, code, pkce_verifier, dpop_proof) -> Result<reqwest::Response, PdsClientError>` (returns raw response for caller nonce-retry), `build_pds_authorize_url(metadata, request_uri, login_hint?) -> String` (constructs browser redirect URL), `fetch_audit_log(did) -> Result<String, PdsClientError>` (fetches PLC operation audit log as raw JSON from `{plc_directory_url}/{did}/log/audit`), `post_plc_operation(did, operation) -> Result<(), PdsClientError>` (POSTs signed PLC operation JSON to `{plc_directory_url}/{did}`), `describe_server(pds_url) -> Result<DescribeServerResponse, PdsClientError>` (GET `com.atproto.server.describeServer` — probes an arbitrary PDS for its `did`/available-user-domains before migration), `create_session(pds_url, identifier, password, auth_factor_token?) -> Result<CreateSessionResponse, PdsClientError>` (POST `com.atproto.server.createSession` — the claim flow's password source login; a 401 maps to `PdsClientError::InvalidCredentials`, or `AuthFactorTokenRequired` when the account has email 2FA and no code was supplied; the returned JWTs feed `OAuthClient::new_bearer`). Module-level XRPC functions (take `&OAuthClient`): the claim helpers `request_plc_operation_signature(client)`, `sign_plc_operation(client, request)`, `get_recommended_did_credentials(client)`; and the outbound-migration helpers `get_service_auth(client, aud, lxm)`, `create_account_migration(client, request)` (maps HTTP 409 → `PdsClientError::DidAlreadyExists` for resume), `import_repo(client, car_bytes)`, `upload_blob(client, mime, bytes)`, `list_missing_blobs(client, cursor)`, `get_preferences(client)`, `put_preferences(client, prefs)`, `check_account_status(client)`, `activate_account(client)`, `deactivate_account(client)`. Every authenticated XRPC helper routes its non-2xx branch through the private `classify_xrpc_response(context, resp)` (→ pure `classify_xrpc_error(status, retry_after, body)`), so a server response is classified by status — `429 → RateLimited{retry_after}`, `401 → Unauthorized`, else `XrpcError{status, error, message}` carrying the atproto error envelope — instead of being flattened into `NetworkError` (MM-290). `NetworkError` is now transport-only. Types: `PlcDidDocument` (Clone), `PlcService` (Clone), `AuthServerMetadata`, `PdsParResponse`, `SignPlcOperationRequest`, `SignPlcOperationResponse`, `RecommendedCredentials`, plus migration types `DescribeServerResponse`, `ServiceAuthToken`, `CreateAccountMigrationRequest`, `CreateAccountResponse`, `CreateSessionResponse`, `MissingBlob`/`MissingBlobs`, `UploadBlobResponse`, `AccountStatus` (from `checkAccountStatus`). `PdsClientError` enum: HANDLE_NOT_FOUND, DID_NOT_FOUND, PDS_UNREACHABLE, NETWORK_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED, UNAUTHORIZED, XRPC_ERROR, INVALID_RESPONSE, OAUTH_FAILED, DID_ALREADY_EXISTS, INVALID_CREDENTIALS, AUTH_FACTOR_TOKEN_REQUIRED, INSECURE_PDS_URL (serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }`)
- `src/plc_monitor.rs` — PLC monitoring module: `PlcMonitor` (borrows `PdsClient`; `check_all()` iterates all managed DIDs, `check_for_changes(did)` diffs current audit log against cached log and classifies new entries as authorized/unauthorized by verifying signatures against the device key); `run_monitoring_loop(app_handle)` (spawned once at app startup, checks every 15 minutes via `tokio::time::interval` with `MissedTickBehavior::Delay`, emits `"plc_alert"` Tauri event to frontend when unauthorized changes detected); `check_identity_status` (Tauri IPC command: synchronous foreground check of all managed identities, returns `Vec<IdentityStatus>`). Types: `UnauthorizedChange` { cid, created_at, signing_key, operation } (camelCase serialization), `IdentityStatus` { did, alert_count, unauthorized_changes } (camelCase serialization), `MonitorError` { NetworkError, IdentityStoreError, ParseError } (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE tag serialization)
- `src/agents.rs` — Agent consent + audit module (5 **per-identity** Tauri IPC commands, the wallet side of the auth.md claim ceremony + "My agents"): `preview_agent_claim(did, user_code) -> AgentClaimPreview` (POST `/v1/agents/claim-preview` — what approving would grant, shown before the biometric gate), `confirm_agent_claim(did, user_code) -> AgentClaimConfirmation` (POST `/agent/identity/claim/confirm` — the human gate; the frontend wraps it in `authenticateBiometric()`), `list_agents(did) -> Vec<AgentSummary>`, `revoke_agent(did, registration_id)`, `get_agent_audit(did, registration_id, cursor?) -> AgentAuditPage`. Each takes a `did` and resolves a **refreshable per-DID full-access session** via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` (like `app_passwords.rs`) — issuing the request through `session.client` (`OAuthClient`), so an expired session self-heals via `refreshSession` or, failing that, `SESSION_LOCKED{reason}` cues the frontend to run the biometric `sovereignLogin(did)` and retry. This replaces the previous auth on the never-refreshed global `"session-token"`, whose lapse dead-ended every agent command as a bogus connection error. Request cores are `_impl` functions taking `&OAuthClient`, tested against httpmock. `AgentsError` (NOT_AUTHENTICATED, CODE_NOT_FOUND, CODE_EXPIRED, ALREADY_CLAIMED, ACCESS_DENIED, AGENT_NOT_FOUND, RATE_LIMITED, SESSION_LOCKED, NETWORK_ERROR, UNKNOWN) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }`; the ceremony's `{error}` codes map onto it in `map_ceremony_error`, and a session-lifecycle failure via `map_session_error` (only a genuine transport failure is NETWORK_ERROR — a NeedsUnlock is SESSION_LOCKED, every other verdict is UNKNOWN), so denial/expiry/lock render as explicit states
- `src/oauth_consent.rs` — Wallet-confirmed OAuth consent client (3 **per-identity** Tauri IPC commands, the wallet side of the pending-authorization primitive — Phases A + B of the wallet-confirmed-OAuth-consent design plan): `preview_oauth_consent(did, user_code) -> ConsentPreview` (resolves the selected DID's hosting PDS via `discover_pds`, `GET /oauth/authorize/consent-request?user_code=…` — what approving would grant: client name/id, redirect URI, requesting origin/IP, requested scope list, `login_hint` — shown before the biometric gate), `preview_oauth_consent_by_request_id(did, request_id) -> ConsentPreview` (Phase B QR-scan path: same preview, queried on the `request_id` dimension — the wallet extracts only the `request_id` from the scanned QR and re-verifies it server-side, never trusting QR contents for display; both share one `preview_oauth_consent_impl(did, query_key, query_value)` core), and `confirm_oauth_consent(did, request_id, client_id, decision, granted_scope) -> ConsentDecision` (signs the canonical `crypto::encode_oauth_consent_envelope` — server DID from `describe_server`, account DID, per-DID device key, `request_id`, `client_id`, decision, granted-scope hash, timestamp, nonce — with the DID's device key and POSTs `/oauth/authorize/approve`). Mirrors `sovereign_session.rs` exactly (per-DID key resolved before any request, `pds_url_is_safe`, DID-doc match); the frontend gates `confirmOAuthConsent` behind `authenticateBiometric()`, so a cancelled prompt signs and sends nothing. Request cores are `_impl` functions taking `&PdsClient`, tested against httpmock. `ConsentError` (IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, UNSUPPORTED_HOST, REQUEST_NOT_FOUND, APPROVAL_REJECTED, ALREADY_RESOLVED, RATE_LIMITED, TRANSPORT_FAILURE, KEYCHAIN_FAILURE, SIGNING_FAILED, DID_MISMATCH, SERVER_MISMATCH, INVALID_RESPONSE, SERVER_FAILURE) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` with camelCase fields
- `src/app_passwords.rs` — App-password management (3 Tauri IPC commands — the "sign the official Bluesky app into a passwordless sovereign account" surface): `create_app_password(did, name, privileged) -> AppPasswordCreated` (mints via `com.atproto.server.createAppPassword`; the returned secret is surfaced ONCE — the frontend gates the call behind `authenticateBiometric()`), `list_app_passwords(did) -> Vec<AppPasswordEntry>` (metadata only), `revoke_app_password(did, name)` (server deletes the credential + its sessions/refresh tokens atomically). All three resolve a per-DID full-access session via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` (the PDS routes require full access — an app password cannot manage app passwords); a `NeedsUnlock` maps to `SESSION_LOCKED{reason}`, the frontend's cue to run `sovereignLogin(did)` and retry, mirroring `handle_change.rs`.
